assets.title: 星环下，尚未消失的世界
assets.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: standalone cinematic story artwork for the science-fiction exploration game 远星协议 / EXO: Beneath the Echo. A single polished, very wide landscape image, approximately 16:9, full bleed, no collage, no frame, no captions, no writing, no UI, no logos or watermark. Premium realistic game key art with meticulously designed hard-surface machinery, tangible worn materials, convincing scale, atmospheric perspective, fine cinematic grain, controlled highlights, beautiful legible compositions. The setting is ECHO-9, a rocky moon beneath an immense pale ringed gas giant. Visual language: warm human amber lighting against mineral teal and desaturated blue shadows; solemn, emotional, hopeful, not generic neon cyberpunk. Create a genuine finished image, not an illustrated design sheet.
Scene: Thousands of years before humanity, the ancient civilization on ECHO-9 at the height of its peaceful life. A magnificent coastal city curves around an actual quiet ocean; enormous slender organically engineered stone-and-metal arches, suspended railways tracing coastal mountains, lush terraced gardens; intricate integrated infrastructure rather than random spires. The same pale ringed giant fills part of the sky in credible celestial scale; its ring casts a long shadow over the far sea. In the intimate foreground, two small elegantly nonhuman parent-and-child silhouettes stand at a weathered balcony railing, looking toward tiny warm windows across the harbor. Their simple physical gesture is tender: the adult lowers a hand, the child reaches up. A subtle architectural motif of two almost-touching incomplete rings appears integrated into the balcony. The architecture should feel inhabited and meaningful, not an abandoned ruin. Golden dusk, sea mist, lights just turning on; immense civilization and fragile ordinary life in one frame. Camera: slightly elevated wide 28mm establishing shot; foreground figures small but visibly connected, city layered across the depth; rich readable surface detail. Emotional intention: the beautiful everyday world that will one day be lost. No destruction, no weapons, no human mechs in this ancient period.

Scene: The last civilian evacuation from the HELIOS ground hangar into the underground, year 2188. Camera at human eye level, 35mm cinematic medium-wide framing. In the foreground, a weary East Asian woman teacher in practical worn grey-olive colony workwear kneels to fasten a small child's oxygen-pack harness. Her cuff carries tiny indistinct hand-marked lines, not readable text. The child clutches a modest potted green seedling close to the chest; a second child quietly holds the teacher's sleeve. Faces subtle and believable, fatigue and restrained fear, no theatrical screaming. Behind them, an older mechanic with grease-stained hands checks a transport carriage's heavy safety latch. A line of tired colonists carrying blankets, tools and oxygen cylinders boards the rail transport into an enormous cavern entrance. A 9-meter-tall original humanoid exploration mech stands protectively in the midground, its gun rack removed and replaced by oxygen canisters: ivory ceramic armor, navy torso, muted crimson chest inset, two slender swept-back antenna fins, green-cyan visor, exposed graphite joints, long athletic legs, mechanically credible hands and backpack thrusters. Overhead hangar gantries and scarred industrial detail. A rail route with a few small cyan guidance lamps recedes into darkness. Dim warm emergency lights illuminate faces; cold teal cavern depth. One monumental hangar door remains partially open behind them, showing a sliver of the ringed giant. The composition is about ordinary people caring for each other while a home is abandoned, not a battle tableau. No gore.

Scene: The seventh exploration fleet's final stand, year 2189, viewed from inside a damaged escape-launch bay aboard the flagship. Intimate foreground and enormous space-war scale behind. At right foreground, Captain Shen Yan, a tired East Asian man in his late forties with short greying hair, a practical dark navy officer pressure suit with a narrow orange shoulder accent, stands on the station side of a thick sealed glass launch-pod window. He presses one bare hand quietly to the glass; on the other side, seen mostly from behind, a young adult helmeted pilot in an ivory-and-graphite flight suit raises a gloved hand to meet it through the glass. Both anatomically natural hands, no exaggerated expression; his face resolute and painfully human. A 9-meter ivory/navy/crimson humanoid AEGIS exploration mech is visibly secured deeper in the launch cradle behind the pilot, with swept-back paired antennae, cyan visor, precise paneling and flight thrusters. Through the far hangar opening in the left background: the pale ringed gas giant, the flagship's damaged armored hull, a few small rescue craft escaping under its protection, distant blue-white weapon beams and one controlled orange explosion. Torn cables, drifting tiny debris, warm emergency lamps; keep the foreground crystal clear and background cinematic. The captain is staying behind. Emphasize separation by glass, sacrifice, a quiet unfinished farewell. No giant fireball swallowing the people, no readable text, no gore.

Scene: After the crash, the player's EV-04 AEGIS stands at the threshold of a huge explorable layered-rock canyon and ancient underground passage at dusk. Hero environment key art. Single original 9-meter-tall humanoid mecha in full-body three-quarter rear view, placed slightly left of center: athletic human proportions, narrow waist, long articulated legs, broad layered shoulder armor, ivory ceramic plate with navy undersuit and restrained crimson inserts, graphite exposed pistons and joints, paired slim swept-back antenna fins, small cyan visor, compact twin flight thrusters with only a faint resting glow. Armor dusty, scratched and lovingly engineered, grounded weight and natural pose, head turned toward the cave as if listening. Beam-saber hilt stowed at hip, no weapon raised. A trail of tiny cyan maintenance lamps winds over a worn vehicle ramp from the robot into the immense cavern, passing an abandoned colonist transport and a small lit shelter; warm amber cabin light implies someone may still be alive. In the deep rock, partly visible monumental alien metal structures bear two incomplete interlocking circular motifs, mysterious rather than obvious exposition. On the right and across the upper background, the canyon opens to a magnificent pale gas giant and immense ring spanning a cold dusk sky. Smooth eroded strata, granular dust, distinct rocks and human-size handrails establish scale; sharp foreground material detail, misty layered distance. The scene must feel lonely but profoundly hopeful: somebody left the lights on. Compose spaciously for future game title overlays, but generate no text. Do not make the robot a tiny anonymous speck; legible hero design with an enormous world beyond.
